text:
sam: Heads up — tried installing redwoodctl inside WSL via winget on a corp laptop. Installer completed but the cli can't find creds after auth.

sam: Sequence: `winget install --id Redwood.RedwoodCtl` then `redwoodctl auth login` (browser opens on Windows). Login completes but `redwoodctl whoami` in WSL shows not logged in.

claire: Winget/Windows installers usually write to %LOCALAPPDATA% by default. If the binary is a Windows exe, it will also write config to Windows paths. WSL running a Linux shell won't automatically read that.

sam: Is there any magic detection in the CLI to prefer $HOME in WSL? I expected it so we could use the same binary from both sides.

vasu: We had a similar report. Current behavior: if CLI is a native Windows exe it uses the Windows appdata. If native Linux binary, uses XDG config. We don't currently translate/mirror creds.

mika: Short-term workaround: run `redwoodctl auth login --device` from WSL and paste the code in a browser. That will create `~/.redwood/profiles.json` and work as expected.

sam: Device flow works, thanks. But some new engineers will just follow the Windows install doc and be confused. Could we add an install-time prompt that offers to create a tiny shim in /usr/local/bin when running under WSL?

vasu: Good suggestion. We can detect WSL via `/proc/version` or `WSL_INTEROP` env var. Option: installer could offer `Create WSL shim (y/n)` and write a wrapper script that proxies to the Windows exe, or better: install the Linux binary inside WSL when detected.

claire: For the wrapper: something like:
```
#!/bin/bash
/mnt/c/Users/you/AppData/Local/Programs/Redwood/redwoodctl.exe "$@"
```
Make it executable and put in `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` so PATH resolves to it.

sam: I tried a symlink to the exe (`ln -s /mnt/c/Users/you/Programs/redwood/redwoodctl.exe /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl`) and got `permission denied` when creating the symlink (root needed) and then `Exec format error` when trying to run it directly. The bash wrapper approach avoids that.

mika: Exec format error is expected if kernel tries to execute a PE file directly. The wrapper executes the Windows exe via WSL interop, so it works.

vasu: Filed DEVEX-4421: "installer should detect WSL and offer Linux shim or install linux binary" with reproduction steps and proposed patch.

dev-tools-bot: New ticket created: DEVEX-4421  CLI: WSL install path and credentials mismatch - offer shim or linux package. Assigned to @vasu.

sam: Additional ask: if the CLI writes to Windows path, can we mirror credentials to `~/.redwood` as well? That would make both environments happy.

vasu: Mirroring is doable but we need to be careful about race conditions and file permissions. My plan in the PR: when detecting WSL and a Windows-style path, write a small symlink file and a JSON mirror with sticky metadata. Also add a `redwoodctl config sync-paths` command to force sync between stores.

claire: Nice. Also add a note in the quickstart: "If using WSL, prefer `redwoodctl auth login --device` or install the Linux package inside your distro."

sam: Verified local build from vasu's branch: `auth login --device` now creates `~/.redwood/profiles.json` in WSL and `whoami` works. The shim installer option is working too. Thanks all :thumbsup:
